text:
ivan-sales: Streamline Health POC finished the perf run this morning. Quick summary in-thread please — they asked for a short customer-facing latency line, and want to see multi-region failover behavior + a tiny CSV for p50/p95/p99. cc @nora-eng @lee-sre @courtney-se

streamline-rep: Ran three scenarios: baseline steady (150 r/s), night spike (520 r/s for 90s), and simulated primary-region outage -> failover to secondary region (steady 150 r/s but higher infra latency). Artifacts: https://s3.company/internal/poc/streamline/2176/report.zip

nora-eng: Commands used (k6):
```
k6 run --vus 160 --duration 6m --rps 150 script.js    # baseline
k6 run --vus 600 --duration 5m --rps 520 spike.js     # spike
// POST /v1/generate, max_tokens=256, stream=false
```

lee-sre: High-level numbers from my scrape of the results (256-token gen):
- Baseline (150 r/s): p50=30ms, p95=165ms, p99=360ms, errors 0.1%
- Spike (520 r/s, 90s): p50=37ms, p95=530ms, p99=1.6s, errors 0.9% (TCP resets on a hot pod)
- Failover (primary gone -> secondary): p50=60ms, p95=420ms, p99=950ms, errors 0.3% (adds inter-region hop + DNS convergence)

courtney-se: They want a one-liner we can put in their SOW and also a bullet note for the architecture slide about failover tradeoffs. Any suggestions?

nora-eng: Suggested blurb for SOW: "On dedicated pools sized for your sustained throughput, expect p95 latency of ~165ms for a 256-token generation (measured on a 3B-class model). Short bursts above provisioned QPS may increase p99; we recommend burst pools and tuned autoscale policies to limit tail latency."

ivan-sales: That reads well. Add a parenthetical: (multi-region failover can increase p50 due to inter-region traffic).

streamline-rep: Also flagged cost question: if we keep a warm burst pool for 5% of peak QPS what is rough cost delta? They want a ballpark.

lee-sre: Ballpark: warm burst pool sized at 5% peak adds roughly 8-12% to GPU-hour cost depending on instance type. I'll give a tightened estimate if they share desired peak instance types.

ivan-sales: Can we promise automatic fallback to smaller quantized model to save cost during sustained load? They asked if we can do this automatically.

nora-eng: Default recommendation: don't auto-fallback without a quality gate. We can provide an automated fallback with constraints: run fallback only if (1) recent quality metric drop < X, (2) sustained overload > Y seconds, and (3) customer opt-in. We'll include a short checklist for evaluations.

courtney-se: Security check: SQA wants to confirm load tests used synthetic data and that logs were scrubbed. Please confirm.

streamline-rep: Confirmed: synthetic prompts only; we masked all IDs and scrubbed logs before upload. No customer PII processed.

deploy-bot: infra: scaled nodes 4 -> 9 @ 2176123560 (autoscale triggered, cooldown=18s)

lee-sre: Observations and recommended mitigations:
- Load-balancer queueing observed once traffic passed ~420 r/s; reduce LB queue depth for predictable tail or add burst pool.
- Autoscaler lag was ~16-22s before pods became ready; recommend cooldown=10s for bursty apps and pre-warm strategy.
- For multi-region failover, add DNS TTL trickle and client-side retry policy to avoid spike at secondary region.

ivan-sales: Can someone export a tiny CSV for the deck: scenario,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms ? Need it by EOD to update slides.

nora-eng: I'll drop csv to S3: /streamline/2176/p99_csv.csv by 2176123720. It will contain:

baseline,30,165,360
spike,37,530,1600
failover,60,420,950

courtney-se: Draft security blurb for the customer: "All POC testing used synthetic prompts only; no production data or PII was ingested. Logs shared with Redwood were scrubbed prior to upload."

ivan-sales: Perfect. Final action items:
- (nora) upload CSV + small graph -> by 2176123720
- (lee) tighten cost delta estimate for a 5% warm pool -> by 2176123750
- (courtney) add quality-gate template for auto-fallback -> by 2176123800

ivan-sales: Thanks team — if deliverables land we can send the consolidated deck + SOW by tomorrow morning. :rocket:
